question: In India, secondary lymphoedema due to filariasis (caused by Wuchereria bancrofti transmitted by Culex mosquitoes) is a leading cause of lower limb lymphoedema and presents with progressive painless limb swelling that pits initially but becomes non-pitting in the fibrotic stage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Wuchereria bancrofti, transmitted by the Culex mosquito, causes lymphatic obstruction leading to lymphoedema. In tropical India, filariasis is the most common cause of secondary lymphoedema. Early disease shows pitting oedema; chronic fibrosis leads to non-pitting brawny oedema and eventually elephantiasis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Filariasis is the most common cause of secondary lymphoedema worldwide and a major cause in India. The filarial worms obstruct lymphatics, causing progressive oedema that begins as pitting (early) and becomes non-pitting brawny oedema (late fibrotic stage). Treatment includes diethylcarbamazine, limb elevation, compression, and hygiene.
